assets.role: Derived pose export — common baseline, uniform bounding-box height
assets.provenance: Derived from the originals in brand/poses/ by tools/normalize-poses.mjs. Originals unmodified.
assets.tool: headless Chromium canvas (no image library on this host)
assets.license: Derived from the pose originals; same terms.
assets.notes:
**Does less than it was built to do, and the measurement says so.** It gives all seven poses a common baseline and a uniform 1000px content height. It does NOT give them a uniform character scale: head-width spread measured 49.2% before and 49.1% after, i.e. unchanged. Scaling by bounding box cannot fix character scale, because a seated pose stretched to the same height as a standing one simply gets a bigger head.

The premise was also partly wrong. The five in-app contract states are driven by brand/frog-mark.svg, not by these PNGs, so nothing swaps these in place rapidly — they are illustrations for larger placements. Scale variance across them is therefore a cosmetic inconsistency, not the defect it was first called.

Kept because a common baseline is genuinely useful if a pose ever goes in a fixed-size slot. True character-scale consistency is best fixed at generation time, or by hand against the head width; an automatic top-band proxy is unreliable for poses with raised arms, which is why `browse` measures 487 and `completion` 815.
